sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The common snapdragon is a perennial subshrub, often grown as an annual, native to northern Spain and south-central to eastern France. It reaches roughly 20–100 cm in cultivation; its two-lipped flowers have a closed, hinged-looking opening. Flower colour and size vary widely among cultivars.

sections.title: Uses and food
sections.text: It is chiefly cultivated as an ornamental. Kew records food use, but this does not establish that every garden cultivar or treated plant is suitable to eat; the plate's vivid colour is not a species-wide trait.

sections.title: Related research plant
sections.text: Arabidopsis thaliana belongs to Brassicaceae, whereas snapdragon is Plantaginaceae. Both are used to study flower development, but are distantly related and differ greatly in flower form and plant size.
